# Derived Hom from Compact Spaces to Real Banach Spaces　`ex.chaus-banach-rhom`

[in graph](../#n=ex.chaus-banach-rhom)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./ex.chaus-banach-rhom.md)

## Notes · **draft**
**Intuition**: $\mathbb{Z} \cdot S$ is the free abelian group generated by $S$; a group homomorphism from it to $N$ is "assign to each point of $S$ an element of $N$". Requiring it to be **continuous** gives exactly the continuous function space $C(S, N)$.

**Why only degree 0**: $\mathbb{Z} \cdot S$ is projective when $S$ is compact Hausdorff, and projective objects have no higher Ext.

⭐ This is the **local computation** behind the step "real Banach is acyclic on compact Hausdorff spaces": every cell of the spectral sequence has this shape.
